lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to World 16, the Ruins of Memory. Last time, the wind feather showed us old stone ruins on the map. And now we are here! Look at these old walls and this tall tower. Long, long ago, people lived here. Today's sentence is: People lived here long ago. Say it with me. People lived here long ago. Great! Lived is the past form of live. We use past forms for things that already happened. このワールドでは「すぎた こと」を たくさん はなすよ。 Long ago means a very long time before now. Now, phonics. Live, lived. Like, liked. Dance, danced. Smile, smiled. These words end in e, so we just add d. Easy, right? Here's a tip. Ruins are very old and easy to break, so we touch them gently. Let's be careful explorers. Ready? Let's explore the ruins!

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! We're at the entrance of the ruins. Before we go in, let's talk about yesterday. To ask about yesterday, say, What did you do yesterday? Say it with me. What did you do yesterday? Great! Did is the past form of do. In the answer, we use a past form. I played soccer with my friends. I tried a new food. It was good! きのうの ことは did で きいて、played の ような すぎた かたちで こたえるよ。 Now, phonics. Cry, cried. Try, tried. Carry, carried. Study, studied. When a word ends in a consonant and y, change the y to i and add ed. Let's spell cried together. C, r, i, e, d. Good! Here's a tip. When your friend answers, ask one more question, like, Was it fun? Then it's a real conversation. Okay, let's ask our friends about yesterday!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, explorers! We're walking inside the ruins. It's a little dark, so we have flashlights. Suddenly, Riko says, Stop! There's a big painting on the wall. Later, we can say, We stopped and looked at the wall. Say it with me. We stopped and looked at the wall. Great! You can join two past actions with and. Stopped and looked. Walked and talked. Now, phonics. Stop, stopped. Clap, clapped. Hop, hopped. Drop, dropped. These words have a short vowel and end in one consonant. So we double the last letter and add ed. 2つ かさねる ルールは -ing の ときと おなじだね。 Here's a tip. In a dark place, walk slowly and stay with your group. Don't run! Okay, let's look at the painting together. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We're in a long, dark passage in the ruins. Shh! What was that? Something moved! To ask a friend, say, Did you see that? Say it with me. Did you see that? Good! For a yes answer, say, Yes, I did. For a no answer, say, No, I didn't. Didn't means did not. Did ～? の しつもんには、Yes, I did. か No, I didn't. で こたえるよ。 Let's try one more. Did you hear a noise? No, I didn't. Now, phonics. Today we mix all the rules. Jump, jumped. Just add ed. Wave, waved. Just add d. Hug, hugged. Double the g. Hurry, hurried. Change y to i. Here's a tip. If you see a small wild animal, don't touch it. Just watch it quietly. Okay, let's find out what moved!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Our first day at the ruins is over. Tonight, let's write a ruins diary in the tent. In a diary, we write about things that already happened, so we use past forms. Today's sentences are: We walked to the ruins. We found a door. Say them with me. We walked to the ruins. We found a door. Great! Walked has ed, but found is a special past form. Find, found. 日記は すぎた ことだから、すぎた かたちで かくよ。 You can also use was and were. It was dark, but we weren't scared. Weren't means were not. Now, phonics review. Walked. Arrived. Clapped. Carried. Remember the four ed rules! Here's a tip. In a diary for sharing, you don't need to write your real name or address. Okay, let's read our diaries to each other!

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! Last night, we all made a campfire together in the plaza. Do you remember? Today's sentence is: We sang a song by the campfire. Say it with me. We sang a song by the campfire. Wonderful! Sang is the past form of sing. Some verbs don't use ed. They change their spelling instead. sing の すぎた かたちは singed では なく、sang だよ。 Now, phonics. Sing, sang. Swim, swam. Drink, drank. Ring, rang. Can you hear it? The i changes to a. Let's say them again quickly. Sang, swam, drank, rang! Great! You can also ask a friend, Did you sing, too? Yes, I did. Here's a tip. A campfire is very hot, so always make one with a grown-up. Never play with fire. Okay, let's talk about our campfire night!
